column1: # Latvian grammar words. One line per word as written + part of speech:
# word <TAB> UD part of speech <TAB> senses separated by " | ".
# The file replaces Wiktionary's determiner, pronoun, preposition, conjunction,
# particle and auxiliary entries for every word listed here; nouns, verbs,
# adverbs and other content words stay (ir "is" the verb, tā "so").
# A line with a content part of speech (protams ADV) replaces Wiktionary's
# entry of that part of speech for the word; X lines only add.
# Other spellings after a "/" find the line too: the forms of a word Wiktionary
# lacks (nosaukums/nosaukuma/nosaukumu), since the protocol has no inflection
# Written without a reader of the language (see profile.md): every line is the
# developer's, checked against the dump and the corpus, not by a Latvian reader.
# Each sense explains what the word does, for a learner reading it next to
# the sentence: what it expresses, then the English, then a short phrase in
# brackets when the English alone doesn't settle it ("with a dative, has: I
# have a dog (man ir suns)"). No notes on case: the sentence shows those.
# A form names its base word, which links it: "form of būt: was → būt".
# The second half holds common words English Wiktionary has no Latvian entry
# for at all (savukārt, nosaukums, pieņemt): hand patches, each with the
# forms a reader meets. They are on profile.md's hand-patch list.
# Wiktionary gives these as "third-person singular present indicative of
# būt": is. A reader also needs what they do with another word: there is,
# I have (man ir), and the perfect (ir izdarījis "has done").
# Wiktionary's `ir` conjunction and particle ("also, even", `ir ... ir`
# "both ... and") are left out: a reader of everyday Latvian doesn't meet them,
# and they took second place in the popover of one of the commonest words.
